threads.body: After a successful SDK manager exit, `SyncStreamManagerWrapper` still calls `stream_wrapper.__exit__` at line 771, closing a stream that the [SDK manager already closed](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/8baaef1c4d23b2e4861d05da0dca65252e879eb8/src/anthropic/lib/streaming/_messages.py#L193-L199). If only that second close raises, this new guard replaces the caller's exception with an instrumentation-only failure; the async path has the same issue at lines 369–370 and 842. After successful manager cleanup, call `_finalize_failure(exc_val)` for an unsuppressed caller error or `_finalize_success()` otherwise, without closing again, and add sync/async regression tests where only the second close fails.
threads.hunk:
@@ -237,6 +237,10 @@ def __exit__(
                 try:
                     self._self_stream.close()
                 except Exception:  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
+                    # A stream that isn't a context manager (e.g. a generator)
+                    # would never be closed here without instrumentation.
+                    if hasattr(self._self_stream, "__exit__"):
+                        raise

replies.body: Good catch, fixed in 78637afc9: after a clean manager exit we now finalize without closing again. Added sync/async regression tests.

Both exceptions are `RuntimeError`, so the `error.type` assertion below passes whichever one the span records. With a distinct type for the close error the test still passes (py311 openai-latest), and it pins that the span keeps the caller's `RuntimeError` while the caller sees `OSError`:

```suggestion
            raise OSError("close failure")

        monkeypatch.setattr(response.__wrapped__, "close", close_raises)
        with pytest.raises(OSError, match="close failure") as raised:
```

`__exit__` calls `_finalize_failure(exc_val)` before closing, so the split looks intentional rather than accidental.
